items.question: How long does it take to build an agent?
items.answer: A working first version usually takes less than a month. Getting it into production with your data, permissions and approvals takes around three months. From there it grows with your needs.

items.question: What return can we expect, and how do you measure it?
items.answer: Before we build anything, we measure how long the task takes today and how often it runs. After launch we measure again. The return is the time saved multiplied by the cost of that time, minus what the agent costs to run. If the numbers do not justify an agent, we tell you.

items.question: Do you build custom agents or use ready-made ones?
items.answer: Both. Where a ready-made tool does the job, we set it up and connect it. Where your process is specific, we build a custom agent around it. The choice depends on what gets you the result fastest and cheapest.

items.question: Where is our data processed, and is it used for training?
items.answer: We use enterprise AI plans whose terms exclude training on your data. Where your rules require it, we host models and data on infrastructure you control. Processing follows the GDPR, and we document where every piece of data goes.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We monitor the agent, fix what breaks and improve it as your process changes. You can keep us on a support plan or take it over fully.

items.question: Can our team maintain the agents ourselves?
items.answer: Yes. We work alongside your team, document everything and train the people who will own the agent, so you are never locked in.

faq.title: Questions about AI strategy and consulting

items.question: What do you need from our side?
items.answer: Time with the people who do the work, not only with management, plus access to the tools and sample documents they use every day. We keep interviews short and work around your team's schedule.

items.question: What do we have at the end?

items.question: Do we have to build the projects with you afterwards?

items.question: What is the difference between an agent and a chatbot?
items.answer: A chatbot answers questions. An agent works through a task step by step: it collects documents, checks figures against your systems and prepares the result, such as a draft entry or a report, for a person to approve.

items.question: What if the agent gets something wrong?
items.answer: It is built so mistakes are caught before they matter. The agent can only take the actions we give it, every figure points to its source, and a person approves anything that leaves the company. Before handover, a reviewer outside the build team tests it on real cases from your own files.

items.question: How long until a first agent runs?
items.answer: We aim for a working first version on one process within a month, and production within about three. It depends mostly on how easy your systems are to connect and how clean the data is.

faq.title: Questions about chatbots and company assistants

items.question: What happens when the assistant does not know the answer?
items.answer: It says so instead of guessing, and passes the question to the right person with the conversation attached. Those unanswered questions also show you which documents are missing or out of date.

items.question: How do the answers stay current when our documents change?
items.answer: The assistant reads from the folders and systems where your documents already live. When a policy or price list is updated there, the next answer uses the new version, and retired documents can be removed from its sources.

items.question: Can it answer in Arabic, French and English?
items.answer: Current AI models handle all three, and customers can usually write in the language they prefer. We test with real questions from your customers and staff, including local dialect and mixed languages, before it goes live.

voice-agents.title: AI voice agents
voice-agents.metaTitle: AI voice agents for business phone calls
voice-agents.summary: AI phone agents that answer calls, book appointments, qualify leads and pass the caller to a person when the call needs judgement.
voice-agents.intro: Every missed call is a booking or a customer that may go elsewhere. An AI voice agent picks up the phone, holds a natural conversation and does something useful with it: it books the appointment, takes the details or transfers the call to the right person. We start with one type of call, such as after-hours calls, and widen it only once it has proved itself.

features.title: Books straight into your calendar
features.text: The agent checks free slots, books or reschedules, and texts the caller a confirmation.

features.title: Asks your qualifying questions
features.text: It asks what your sales team always asks and writes the answers into your customer records.

features.title: Transfers with a short summary
features.text: Upset callers, urgent cases and anything that needs judgement go to a person, with the context.

features.title: Open about being AI
features.text: The first sentence tells callers they are speaking to an AI assistant and whether the call is recorded.

useCases: After-hours calls for plumbers and electricians, with emergencies sent to whoever is on call
Bookings, cancellations and earlier-slot requests for dental and physio clinics
Viewing requests and repair reports for property managers
A hotel reservations line in Arabic, French and English

items.question: Can we keep our existing phone number?
items.answer: Yes. The simplest start is to forward calls to the agent only after hours or when nobody answers, so your main line stays as it is. Once the pilot has proved itself, the number can be moved to a provider that connects it to the agent directly.

items.question: Do callers have to be told they are speaking to an AI?
items.answer: In the EU, yes, unless it is already obvious, and today's voices sound human enough that it often is not. We put the disclosure, and the recording notice where calls are recorded, in the first sentence of every call. Rules on recording differ by country, so we check yours before going live.

items.question: Will it understand our callers' accents and dialects?
items.answer: Speech recognition is only as good as what it was trained on, so we do not assume. Before launch we test with recordings of your real callers, including dialect mixed with French or English, and keep a person on the transfer line for anything it does not understand.

faq.title: Questions about AI training for your team

items.question: Do participants need a technical background?
items.answer: No. The programme is written for people who have never built anything with AI. If someone can write an email and use a spreadsheet, they can follow it.

items.question: Which AI tools do participants learn?
items.answer: We train on the tools your company already has or plans to approve, so what people learn works on Monday morning. If nothing is chosen yet, the sessions also help you compare the main options for your needs.

items.question: How do you adapt the programme to our company?
items.answer: Before the sessions, we collect a few real tasks from each team, such as a recurring report or a standard reply. Participants then build their first workflow on those tasks, and the length and format are agreed with you.

process-automation.title: Process automation
process-automation.metaTitle: Business process automation with n8n and Make
process-automation.summary: Workflows that remove copy-paste, retyping and manual hand-offs between email, spreadsheets and the systems your team already uses.
process-automation.intro: Many processes still depend on someone copying data from one screen to another. We map the process as it is, remove the manual steps and connect the systems directly, with AI only where it adds something rules cannot.

features.title: Mapped before it is built

features.title: No more retyping

features.title: Exceptions go to a person
features.text: Anything unusual is flagged and routed to the right colleague.

features.title: Visible and measured

useCases: Order entry from email into your finance and stock system
Supplier onboarding and document checks
Weekly sales and stock reports
Approval workflows that today live in email threads

items.question: Which tools do you build automations with?
items.answer: Often with workflow tools such as n8n or Make, and with custom code when the logic, the volume or a security review calls for it. We choose the tool that fits the people who will look after it, not the one that makes the best demo.

items.question: Can our data stay in Europe or on our own servers?
items.answer: Usually, yes. n8n can run on your own servers or in its hosted service in Frankfurt, and Make offers EU data zones, with some exceptions for its AI features. We check where each step of the workflow sends data before anything goes live.

items.question: What happens when an automation breaks?
items.answer: Every run is logged, and a failed or unusual run alerts a named person instead of failing quietly. We hand over documentation so your team can see how each workflow works, and agree with you who fixes what after launch.

api-integration.title: Connect your existing tools
api-integration.metaTitle: API and MCP integration for your business tools
api-integration.summary: Your existing tools connected to each other and to AI, through secure connectors that only reach the data and actions you approve.
api-integration.intro: AI is only useful when it can see your data and act in your systems, and your systems are more useful when they share information. We build secure connectors between the software you already run and between that software and AI tools, so information flows where it is needed and access stays limited to what you approve.

features.title: Your systems, not new ones
features.text: We connect what you already use: Excel, email, databases, your sales system and your finance and stock software.

features.title: Least access by default

features.title: Standard connectors

features.title: Logged end to end

useCases: Letting your company assistant read your sales and finance systems
Syncing spreadsheets with a central database
Connecting email inboxes to ticketing or order systems
Giving AI tools safe, read-only access to an old in-house system

items.question: What are APIs and MCP, in plain words?
items.answer: An API is a documented door that lets one piece of software talk to another, and most modern business systems have one. MCP is an open standard that works like a universal plug for AI: we build one connector per system, and any compatible AI tool can use it with only the permissions you grant.

items.question: Can you connect an old system that has no API?
items.answer: Usually, yes. We can read from a limited, read-only view of its database, or work from the files it already exports each night. Automating the screens is possible but fragile, so we only use it as a last resort.

items.question: Will AI be able to change data in our systems?
items.answer: Only what you decide, and usually only drafts that a person then confirms. Payments, bank details and master data stay out of reach. Every connector is tested on a copy of your system with test data before it touches the live one, starting with read-only access.

data-platforms.metaTitle: Data warehouse, data cleaning and dashboards
data-platforms.summary: Your data cleaned, brought into one place and turned into dashboards your managers can trust, so every meeting starts from the same figures.
data-platforms.intro: When sales, finance and operations each keep their own spreadsheet, every meeting starts with an argument about whose figure is right. We clean and structure your data, bring it into one central store and build the reports people actually use. It is also the step that comes before AI: an assistant or agent is only as reliable as the data it reads.

features.text: Duplicates, missing values and inconsistent formats are fixed by rules that run on every load, not by hand.

features.title: Dashboards built around decisions

features.title: Every figure traceable

useCases: A monthly management report that builds itself from sales, finance and stock data
One customer list merged from several branches, without duplicates
Replacing a chain of linked spreadsheets that only one person understands
Preparing clean, structured data before launching an AI assistant

faq.title: Questions about data platforms and dashboards

items.question: Our data is messy. Where do we start?
items.answer: With the few figures your managers argue about most, such as revenue, margin or stock. We trace where each one comes from, fix the sources and rules behind it, and widen from there instead of trying to clean everything at once.

items.question: Which dashboard tools do you use?
items.answer: It depends on what your team already has and pays for. If you work in Microsoft 365, Power BI is often the natural choice, and there are open-source options when licence costs matter. The central data store stays independent of the dashboard tool, so you can change one without rebuilding the other.

items.question: Who owns the platform, and who keeps it running?
items.answer: You own the data and the platform, built in your company's own accounts. A Qartmina project lead runs the build, the engineering is done by data specialists we select for the job, and everything is checked by us before handover. We document it so your team can run it, and agree any ongoing support with you.

business-websites.title: Business websites
business-websites.summary: Showcase sites, landing pages and multilingual websites that load fast, read well on phones and are easy for your team to update.
business-websites.intro: A business website has one job: make it easy for the right customer to trust you and get in touch. We plan the structure with you, design it around your brand and build it so pages open quickly on any phone. Your team can then change text, photos and offers without calling a developer.

features.title: Multilingual from day one
features.text: Arabic, French and English versions, with right-to-left layouts where Arabic needs them.

features.title: Edit it yourself
features.text: A simple editor lets your team update pages, news and photos in minutes.

features.title: Fast on mobile data

features.title: Built to be found

A landing page for a product launch or advertising campaign
A trilingual site for a business selling across North Africa and the Gulf
A careers page that collects job applications in one place

items.question: How long does a business website take?
items.answer: A focused showcase site or landing page usually takes a few weeks. The biggest factor is how quickly text, photos and approvals come together. We agree a timeline at the start and tell you early if anything changes it.

items.question: What do you need from us?
items.answer: Your logo and brand colours, a clear idea of who the site is for, and one person who can approve content. If you do not have text or photos yet, we can write the copy with you and plan the images.

items.question: Who owns the website and the domain?
items.answer: You do. The domain is registered in your company's name, and you receive the admin access and source files at handover. If you later choose another provider, you can take everything with you.

web-platforms.summary: Client portals, booking platforms, marketplaces and member areas with logins, payments and links to the systems you already use.
web-platforms.intro: Some websites need to do more than inform. Clients log in to track an order, members book a session, sellers list products, staff approve requests. A members' area with paid content and automatic renewals

items.question: Why not use an off-the-shelf tool?
items.answer: Often you should, and we will tell you when a ready-made product fits. A custom platform makes sense when your process is what sets you apart, or when you have outgrown tools that cannot talk to each other. We compare both options before you commit.

items.question: How do you keep user data secure?
items.answer: Logins, permissions and encryption are designed in from the first week, not added at the end. Personal data is stored only where it is needed and access is logged. Before launch, a security specialist from our vetted network reviews the platform.

items.question: Can we start small and grow?
items.answer: Yes, and we recommend it. We launch a first version with the features that matter most, learn from real users, then add the rest in planned stages.

ecommerce.summary: Online stores built around your catalogue, payments and delivery, with stock kept in sync and payment methods your customers already use.
ecommerce.intro: Store builders work until your catalogue, pricing or delivery rules stop fitting their templates. We build custom online stores for businesses that sell to other businesses, sell across borders, or need the store tied into their own stock and accounting. The store follows your rules, not the other way round.

features.title: Stock that stays accurate
features.text: Every order updates stock levels in your warehouse or accounting system.

features.title: Delivery rules that match reality
features.text: Shipping zones, couriers, pickup points and fees set per city or country.

features.title: Catalogues of any shape
features.text: Variants, bundles, trade pricing and large product ranges without workarounds.

useCases: A wholesaler offering trade prices and bulk orders to registered buyers
A brand selling in several countries with local currencies and languages
A retailer linking its online store to the stock system in its shops
A store adding cash on delivery and mobile payments for local customers

items.question: Should we build a custom store or use Shopify?
items.answer: If your products, pricing and delivery are standard, Shopify is usually faster to launch and simpler to run, and we set that up too. Custom makes sense for trade pricing, complex catalogues, specific local payment needs or deep links to your own systems. We help you decide before any code is written.

items.question: Which payment methods can you connect?
items.answer: It depends on the countries you sell in and the payment providers available there. We look at what your customers actually use, from cards to mobile wallets and cash on delivery, and connect providers that cover them. Your company holds the merchant account, so the money goes straight to you.

items.question: What happens after the store goes live?
items.answer: We stay on for a stabilisation period to fix anything real orders reveal. After that, your team can take over with the training and documentation we hand over, or keep us on a monthly care plan for updates, security and new features.

shopify.title: Shopify stores
shopify.summary: Shopify stores set up properly from the start, or moved from another platform with products, customers and orders intact.
shopify.intro: Shopify is a sound choice for many shops: reliable, secure and simple to run. Getting it right still takes work, from the theme and product data to payments, shipping and the few apps you really need. We set up new stores, move existing ones from platforms such as WooCommerce, Wix or Magento, and train your team to run the shop day to day.

features.title: Theme adapted to your brand
features.text: A proven theme, customised so the store looks like yours and not a template.

features.title: Clean product data
features.text: Products, variants, photos and descriptions imported and checked before launch.

features.title: Only the apps you need
features.text: Each app is chosen for a reason, so monthly fees and slow pages stay in check.

features.title: Migration without broken links
features.text: Old addresses redirect to the new pages, so search rankings and saved links keep working.

useCases: A new brand opening its first online shop
Moving from WooCommerce to Shopify to stop maintaining plugins
Bringing several small shops into one store that serves multiple countries
Training staff to add products, run promotions and handle returns

faq.title: Questions about Shopify setup and migration

items.question: Will we lose customers or orders when we migrate?
items.answer: Not if the move is planned properly. Products, customers and past orders are copied across and counted against the old store before the switch. We go live at a quiet moment and keep the old store available until everything is confirmed.

items.question: Does Shopify work in our country?
items.answer: Shopify works in most countries, but payment options differ from market to market. We check which payment providers work for you and your customers before you commit, and tell you plainly if another platform suits you better.

items.question: Can our team run the store without you?
items.answer: That is the goal. We run hands-on training on your own store and leave a short written guide for everyday tasks. If you want help later, a monthly care plan is available.

website-care.title: Website care and SEO
website-care.summary: Monthly care for your website: hosting, updates, backups, security fixes, speed and the technical work that helps people find you in search.
website-care.intro: A website is not finished at launch. Software needs updates, security holes get discovered, pages slow down and search engines change what they reward. Our monthly care plan handles all of it, including SEO (the technical work that helps search engines find and rank your pages), and you get a plain report of what was done.

features.title: Updates and security fixes
features.text: Software, plugins and themes kept current, with security fixes applied promptly.

features.title: Backups you can restore
features.text: Regular backups stored separately and tested by actually restoring them.

features.title: Speed kept in check
features.text: Load times tracked, with heavy images and slow scripts fixed as they appear.

features.title: Technical search fixes
features.text: Broken links, missing titles, sitemaps and indexing problems found and corrected.

useCases: A company website nobody has updated since it launched
An online store that slowed down after years of added plugins
A site that dropped out of search results after a redesign
Taking over hosting and upkeep from a previous agency

faq.title: Questions about website maintenance and SEO

items.question: What is included each month?
items.answer: Hosting or hosting oversight, updates, backups, uptime monitoring, security fixes and a technical search check. You receive a short monthly report in plain language. Content changes and new features can be added as a set number of hours.

items.question: Can you guarantee first place on Google?
items.answer: Nobody honestly can. We fix the technical issues that stop search engines from reading your site and track how your visibility changes over time. Rankings also depend on your content and your competitors, and we tell you what would help most.

items.question: Can you look after a site another agency built?
items.answer: Yes. We start with an audit of the code, hosting and access, so we know exactly what we are taking on. Every update is then checked by a second person on our side before it reaches your live site.

crm-development.title: CRM development
crm-development.summary: Custom CRMs and tailored HubSpot, Salesforce or Odoo setups that give your sales team one clear view of every customer and deal.
crm-development.intro: A CRM (customer relationship management system) is where your sales team keeps track of customers, contacts and deals. When it is set up badly, people drift back to spreadsheets and notebooks. We configure existing CRMs such as HubSpot, Salesforce or Odoo, or build a custom one when your sales process does not fit them, so the team actually uses it.

features.title: Your sales stages, not defaults
features.text: The pipeline mirrors how your team really wins deals, step by step.

features.title: Contacts cleaned and imported
features.text: Old spreadsheets and address books merged, with duplicates removed before go-live.

features.title: Linked to email and quotes
features.text: Emails, calls and quotes are filed under the right customer without retyping.

features.title: Reports managers trust
features.text: Pipeline, forecast and team activity shown in dashboards built from live data.

useCases: Moving a sales team off shared spreadsheets into one CRM
Cleaning up a HubSpot or Salesforce account nobody trusts any more
A custom CRM for a business that sells through distributors and agents
Linking the CRM to invoicing so sales can see payment status

faq.title: Questions about CRM setup and development

items.question: Should we customise an existing CRM or build our own?
items.answer: Most businesses are better served by configuring a proven CRM, and that is where we start. A custom build makes sense when your sales model is unusual, or when licence costs for a large team outweigh the cost of building. We compare both options for your situation before you decide.

items.question: How do we get the team to actually use it?
items.answer: We involve the people who will use it from the first workshop, keep fields and steps to what they need, and train them on their own deals. Managers take their reports from the CRM, which gives everyone a reason to keep it up to date.

items.question: What happens to our existing customer data?
items.answer: We export it, clean it and import it in stages, checking counts and samples against the original at each step. Nothing old is deleted until you have confirmed the new system is complete.

erp-development.title: ERP development
erp-development.summary: ERP software set up for your finance, stock, purchasing and HR, from Odoo implementation to custom modules and migration off spreadsheets.
erp-development.intro: An ERP (enterprise resource planning system) is the software that runs the back office: accounts, stock, purchasing, payroll and HR in one place. Many growing companies still run these on spreadsheets only one person understands. We implement and customise ERPs, often Odoo, which is widely used in the region, and move your data across without stopping daily operations.

features.title: Process first, software second
features.text: We map how money, stock and approvals move today before configuring anything.

features.title: Modules for local rules
features.text: Custom modules where you need local tax, invoicing or reporting formats.

features.title: Migration in stages
features.text: Opening balances, products and suppliers moved and reconciled one area at a time.

features.title: One set of figures
features.text: Finance, sales and the warehouse all work from the same numbers.

Moving accounting from an old desktop program to a cloud ERP
Extra approval steps for purchase orders above a set amount
Connecting the ERP to the online store and the sales team's CRM

faq.title: Questions about ERP and Odoo projects

items.question: How long does an ERP implementation take?
items.answer: It depends on how many departments go live and how clean your current data is. We usually start with one or two areas, such as stock and purchasing, and add the others once those run smoothly. You get a staged plan with dates before work begins.

items.question: Why Odoo?
items.answer: Odoo covers most back-office needs in one system, is widely used across the region and can be extended with custom modules. It is not always the right fit, and when another ERP suits you better, we say so.

items.question: Who looks after the ERP after go-live?
items.answer: Your team runs it day to day, with training by role and a written guide. We stay on through the first month-end closes, when most questions come up, and can continue with a monthly support plan.

business-apps.title: Business apps and tools
business-apps.metaTitle: Custom business apps and internal tools
business-apps.summary: Internal tools, dashboards and approval apps that replace the spreadsheets and email threads your team uses to run daily work.
business-apps.intro: Most companies run at least one critical process on a spreadsheet passed around by email. It works until two versions disagree or the person who built it leaves. We build focused internal apps that do one job well: collect the data, apply your rules, route approvals and show managers where things stand.

features.title: Forms that check themselves

features.title: Approvals with a trail
features.text: Every request shows who approved it, when and with what comment.

features.title: Dashboards from live data
features.text: Managers see current figures without waiting for someone to compile a report.

features.title: Access by role
features.text: Each person sees and edits only what their job requires.

useCases: Expense claims with receipts, approvals and export to accounting
A quality inspection checklist that replaces paper forms
An operations dashboard combining sales, stock and delivery figures
A contract register that reminds you before renewals fall due

items.question: Why not just improve the spreadsheet?
items.answer: Sometimes that is enough, and we will say so. An app makes sense when several people edit the same data, when approvals matter or when errors are expensive. It keeps one version of the truth and a record of every change.

items.question: How quickly can we have a first version?
items.answer: A tool with one clear job can often reach a first working version within a few weeks, which your team then tests on real work. We improve it in short rounds based on what they report.

items.question: Who owns the code?
items.answer: You do. The code, the data and the accounts it runs on belong to your company, and we document how it all works. A senior engineer on our side reviews every release before your team sees it, so what you inherit is easy to maintain.

mobile-apps.title: Mobile apps
mobile-apps.metaTitle: Mobile app development for iOS and Android
mobile-apps.summary: iOS and Android apps for your customers or field teams, published to the App Store and Google Play and maintained after launch.
mobile-apps.intro: An app earns its place when people need you in their pocket: customers reordering, booking or tracking, or field staff recording visits, deliveries and inspections away from a desk. We design and build apps for iPhone and Android, usually from one shared codebase to keep upkeep simple, publish them to both stores and keep them working as phones change.

features.title: Works with weak signal

features.title: Published under your name

features.title: Notifications that matter
features.text: Order updates and reminders go only to the people they concern.

features.title: Kept current after launch
features.text: We update the app when new iOS and Android versions change the rules.

useCases: A field sales app for taking orders during customer visits
A delivery app with photo and signature proof of delivery
A customer app for reordering and tracking orders
An inspection app for sites with no mobile signal

items.question: Do we need an app, or would a website do?
items.answer: Often a well-built mobile website is enough, and it costs less to run. An app makes sense when people use it every week, need it offline, or rely on the camera, location or notifications. We help you decide before you invest.

items.question: How long until the app is in the stores?
items.answer: Building a first version usually takes a few months, depending on scope. Apple and Google then review each app before it goes live, which can take from a few hours to several days. We prepare the store listings and handle the review process for you.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We watch crash reports and store reviews, fix issues and release updates when Apple or Google change their requirements. You can keep us on a maintenance plan, or your team can take over with full documentation and access.

cloud-migration.title: Cloud migration
cloud-migration.metaTitle: Cloud migration and legacy system modernisation
cloud-migration.summary: Old servers and legacy software moved to the cloud and modernised step by step, while your business and customers keep working.
cloud-migration.intro: Many companies run on software that still works but cannot grow: a server in a cupboard, a system only one developer understands, a disk someone clears by hand every week. We move these systems to the cloud and modernise them in stages, with backups at every step, so the business never has to stop for the change.

features.title: Staged, not all at once
features.text: Data and services move in planned steps, with a short maintenance window only for the final switch.

features.title: Separate test and live systems
features.text: Development and testing get their own data, so nobody experiments on real customer records.

features.title: Automatic checks before release
features.text: Every change runs through the full set of tests before it goes live.

features.title: A way back at every step
features.text: Each stage has a backup and a rollback plan in case anything goes wrong.

useCases: Moving a growing product off a single rented server
Replacing a system on an office server with a cloud version, one module at a time
Moving years of stored files to cloud storage while users keep working
Adding a test environment and release pipeline to an existing product

faq.title: Questions about cloud migration and modernisation

items.question: Will our business have to stop during the move?
items.answer: Not if it is planned well. We move data and services in stages while you keep working, and keep a short, scheduled maintenance window for the final switch. For one software company, we moved about 20 GB of files to cloud storage while its customers kept using the product.

items.question: Do we need to rebuild everything?
items.answer: Rarely. We keep what works, fix what holds you back and replace old parts one at a time. In a recent project the product itself was sound, and the work went into hosting, separating test data from live data and the release process.

items.question: Which cloud providers do you use?
items.answer: We choose based on your needs, your budget and where your data must be stored. We have worked with providers such as AWS, Railway and Cloudflare, and we explain each choice in plain terms. The accounts are in your name, so you are never tied to us.

brand-identity.title: Brand identity and logo
brand-identity.metaTitle: Logo design and brand identity services
brand-identity.summary: A logo, colours, typefaces and simple brand guidelines, so everything your company puts out looks like it comes from the same place.
brand-identity.intro: Your brand is what people remember after seeing your name once. We design your logo, choose your colours and typefaces and write them down in clear guidelines, so your team, your printer and your web developer all use them the same way. If you are still choosing a name, we help you test the options before you commit.

features.title: A logo for every size

features.title: Colours and typefaces chosen

features.title: Guidelines your team can follow

features.title: Naming support

A family business replacing a logo drawn decades ago
Two merged companies that need one identity
A product line launching under its own sub-brand

faq.title: Questions about brand identity and logo design

items.question: How long does a brand identity take?
items.answer: It depends on how many concepts and feedback rounds you want. A logo with core guidelines usually takes a few weeks, and naming adds time if we start there.

items.question: Who owns the logo when the project ends?
items.answer: You do. We hand over all source files and transfer the rights in writing, so you can use and adapt the logo without coming back to us.

items.question: What do you need from us to start?
items.answer: A conversation about who your clients are, what makes you different and which brands you admire or dislike. A decision maker should join the reviews, so the direction does not change late in the project.

graphic-design.title: Graphic design
graphic-design.metaTitle: Graphic design for social media, print and decks
graphic-design.summary: Social media visuals, brochures, signage, pitch decks and packaging, designed to match your brand and ready to publish or print.
graphic-design.intro: Most companies need a steady flow of design work: a post for Monday, a flyer for a trade fair, a deck for an investor meeting. We take that work off your team and deliver files that follow your brand, sized correctly and ready for the printer or the platform. Your project lead checks every file before it reaches you, so you are not the one catching typos.

features.title: Print-ready files

Brochures and roll-up banners for a trade fair stand

Product labels in Arabic and French for a food producer

items.answer: Yes. Send us your logo files and guidelines, or a few examples of what you have published, and we design within them. If you have no guidelines yet, we write a short set as we go.

items.question: Do we get editable files?
items.answer: Yes. You receive the files for print or publishing plus the editable source, in a tool agreed at the start such as Figma, Adobe or PowerPoint. Your team can then make small changes without us.

items.question: Can you handle a regular monthly volume?
items.answer: Yes. Many clients book a set number of designs each month with a turnaround agreed up front. Urgent requests are possible, and we tell you honestly when a deadline is too tight to do well.

ui-ux-design.title: UI/UX design
ui-ux-design.metaTitle: UI/UX design for websites and apps
ui-ux-design.summary: Research, wireframes and clickable prototypes that make your website or app easy to use, tested with real people before anything is built.
ui-ux-design.intro: UX, short for user experience, is how easily someone gets a job done on your website or app. UI, the user interface, is what they see: screens, buttons, text and layout. We talk to your users, sketch the flow, build a prototype people can click through and test it before any code is written, while changes still cost little.

features.title: Research with your real users
features.text: Short interviews and observation sessions show where people get stuck today.

features.title: Wireframes before visuals
features.text: Simple page sketches to agree structure and content before anyone discusses colours.

features.title: Prototypes you can click
features.text: A realistic version of the app you can try on a phone, with no code behind it yet.

features.title: A design system for developers
features.text: Reusable buttons, forms and layout rules, documented so every new screen stays consistent.

useCases: A booking or checkout flow where customers give up before paying
An internal tool staff avoid because every task takes too many clicks
A mobile app idea that needs testing before money goes into development
A website in Arabic and English that must read well right to left

faq.title: Questions about UI and UX design

items.question: Why design before building?
items.answer: Changing a prototype takes hours, changing finished software takes much longer. Testing the design first means your development budget goes into screens people have already shown they can use.

items.question: Can our own developers build from your designs?
items.answer: Yes. We deliver the designs in Figma with sizes, states and notes for each screen, and answer questions while your team builds. If you have no developers, we can build it for you as well.

items.question: Who do you test the designs with?
items.answer: Ideally a handful of your own customers or staff in each round. You help us reach them, and we run the sessions, take notes and share what we learned, with recordings only where people agree.

personal-branding.title: Personal branding
personal-branding.metaTitle: Personal branding for founders and executives
personal-branding.summary: An online presence audit, a link-in-bio page with lead tracking, six months of content with ready assets and a personal website, for founders and executives.

social-media.title: Social media management
social-media.summary: Content plans, posts, AI-generated images and videos, and the automations behind them, so your accounts stay active and your team can run the system.

security-audits.metaTitle: Security audit and vulnerability scanning services
security-audits.summary: Automated and manual checks of your websites, servers and cloud accounts, with a prioritised report in plain language and a re-test after fixes.
security-audits.intro: Many break-ins start with something ordinary: an outdated plugin, a server left open, an old account nobody switched off. A security audit finds these weaknesses before someone else does. We scan and manually check your websites, servers and cloud accounts, then give you a report ranked by risk, written so a manager can decide and a developer can fix. Once the fixes are in, we check again.

features.title: Scans plus manual checks

features.title: A report ranked by risk

items.question: What is the difference between an audit and a penetration test?
items.answer: An audit looks broadly for known weaknesses and wrong settings across your systems. A penetration test goes deeper on a defined target and tries to exploit what it finds, the way an attacker would. Many companies start with an audit.

items.question: Will the scans slow down or break our website?
items.answer: Scans run at times agreed with you and are tuned to avoid heavy load. We confirm in writing which systems are in scope before we start, and we stop at once if anything behaves unexpectedly.

items.question: What do you need from us?
items.answer: A list of the websites, servers and cloud accounts to check, a technical contact and read-only access where we review settings from the inside. We never need your staff's personal passwords.

penetration-testing.title: Penetration testing
penetration-testing.metaTitle: Penetration testing for web apps, APIs and networks
penetration-testing.summary: Authorised, scoped simulated attacks on your web apps, APIs and networks, with a report showing what an attacker could reach and how to close it.
penetration-testing.intro: A penetration test is a controlled attack on your own systems, carried out by a specialist with your written permission. It answers a question scans cannot: if someone really tried, how far would they get? Before any testing, we agree in writing what is in scope, when we test and who to call if something goes wrong. The testing is done by experienced specialists we select for your technology and supervise from start to finish.

features.title: Written authorisation first
features.text: Scope, dates, test accounts and emergency contacts are signed off before the first test.

features.title: Web apps and APIs
features.text: We test logins, permissions and data access, including the APIs, the links your app uses to exchange data with other systems.

features.title: Internal and external networks
features.text: Tested from the internet and, if you choose, from inside your office network, as a staff laptop would see it.

features.title: A report with proof and fixes
features.text: Each finding shows how it was exploited, what it exposes and the steps to close it.

useCases: A customer portal tested before launch
A mobile app checked so one customer can never see another's data
A client asking for a recent penetration test report before signing a contract
An office network tested after a merger or a move

items.question: Is it safe to attack our live systems?
items.answer: Testing is planned to avoid disruption: we agree the times, exclude anything fragile and avoid actions that delete data or overload servers. Where possible we test a copy of your live system. If something unexpected happens, we stop and call your named contact.

items.question: What do we need to prepare?
items.answer: Written authorisation from someone entitled to give it, plus your hosting or cloud provider's approval where their rules require it. Then a scope list, test accounts with different roles and a technical contact during the test window.

items.question: How often should we test?
items.answer: Many companies test once a year and after any major change, such as a new app, a new login system or a move to the cloud. Your clients, your insurer or a standard you follow may set their own requirement.

We find the gaps between how you work today and what the auditor will check, write the policies, help you collect the evidence and prepare your team. faq.title: Questions about security compliance and certification

items.question: Can Qartmina certify us?

items.question: How long does it take to get ready?
items.answer: It depends on your size and on what is already in place. A small company with good habits can move quickly, while one starting from scratch should plan for several months, because some evidence has to build up over time.

items.question: Does this cover GDPR?
items.answer: In large part. GDPR is the European data protection law, and many of the same controls, such as access rights, records and breach procedures, support it. On legal questions we work alongside your lawyer rather than replace them.

ai-security.summary: Permissions, data access, prompt injection testing and human approval, set up for your AI tools and agents before they touch real data.
ai-security.intro: An AI agent that reads email and works in your systems can be tricked by instructions hidden in a document. That trick is called prompt injection, and today it cannot be fully prevented. What you can control is how much damage it could do. We review what your AI tools can read, what they can change and what they can send out, then narrow that access, add human approval for high-impact actions and test the setup the way an attacker would.

features.title: Prompt injection testing

faq.title: Questions about AI and agent security

items.question: What is prompt injection in plain words?
items.answer: It is when someone hides instructions inside content an AI tool reads, such as an email, a PDF or a web page, so the tool follows the attacker instead of you. It works because the AI cannot reliably tell data it should read from orders it should obey.

items.question: Can you make our agent completely safe?
items.answer: No one honestly can, because prompt injection has no complete fix yet. We limit the damage it can do: narrow permissions, separating the agent that reads untrusted content from the one that acts, and human approval for anything that moves money or data.

items.question: When should we do this?
items.answer: Before go-live, while permissions are still easy to change. If an agent is already running, we start from what it can access today and what its logs show it has done.
